title: Profile provenance ledger and anchored-performance publication strategy
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Define and deliver a repeatable publication workflow that produces Redwood-verified performance profiles with immutable provenance metadata and an anchored 'reference' profile per model-variant. These artifacts must be signed, indexable, and usable by the serving runtime for deterministic pinning and automated fallback decisions. The initiative covers profiling methodology, cost normalization, verification harness upgrades, publish API, and operational refresh cadence.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical 'profile manifest' format exists that includes: model hash, runtime build id, hardware family, sequence-length buckets, batching settings, KV-cache warming protocol, median/95th latency, throughput at target concurrency, and normalized cost-per-token.
Profiles published to the registry are signed (artifact signature) and carry a provenance ledger entry recording the test harness, dataset/parquets used, and time-stamped telemetry snapshot.
A single anchored-reference profile is chosen per model-variant and exposed via API for pinning; runtime honors the pin and falls back to pinned-compatible variants when requested.
Publish flow supports staging -> canary -> global transitions with automated smoke checks and rollback hooks.
Cost normalization algorithm implemented and validated across at least 3 region/hardware combos (aws-g5, gcp-a2, onprem-rtx8000).
Docs and quickstart added to the Console and onboarding guides so platform customers can interpret profile fields and pin policies.
milestones: Spec: profile-manifest-v1 (includes provenance schema and signature format) - 2025-03-18
Verification harness upgrades (synthetic load generator, seq-length jitter, KV warmup control) - 2025-03-28
Cost normalization POC and validation across 3 hardware targets - 2025-04-01
Publish API and registry endpoint + staging UI - 2025-04-08
rollout_plan: Stage: ingest legacy profiles and backfill provenance where available; mark as non-anchored if provenance incomplete.
Canary: publish new-style profiles for 10 models to staging registry; run customer-facing queries against staging for 48h.
Monitor: validate telemetry contract (latency/throughput/cost) and manual review of outliers during canary window.
Global: promote anchored profiles when canary meets acceptance criteria; emit signed pins and update catalog.
Post-publish: daily drift checks for first 7 days, then weekly; trigger auto-refresh run if drift threshold crossed.
rollback_criteria: Observed production latency regression >10% for pinned customers within 24h after promotion.
Cost-per-token deviation >15% vs anchored baseline for typical sequences, unexplained by traffic mix.
Verification harness detects repeatable throughput loss on target hardware under canonical load profile.
Manual security or compliance objections surface related to provenance artifacts or signing keys.
telemetry_contracts: Profiles must include raw histogram distributions for latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), not only point estimates.
Throughput measurements must be accompanied by concurrency/queueing backpressure parameters and sample sizes.
Cost normalization: canonical tokenization, token length buckets, and amortized kernel-time accounting fields required.
Each telemetry snapshot must include runtime version, compiler flags, and quantization/weight format metadata.
verification_changes: Add KV-cache warmup scenario to harness (cold/warm/hot) and document expected delta for each bucket.
Introduce seq-length jitter in synthetic generator to better approximate production distribution and avoid overfitting to fixed lengths.
Capture GPU utilization and kernel selection traces and store as part of provenance bundle for debugging regressions.
Automate artifact-signing step in CI and store public keys in registry for attestation verification.
docs_and_training: Console: add 'Profile provenance' tab with human-readable manifest, signature status, and drift history chart.
Onboarding doc: how to interpret normalized cost and pin semantics (TTL, compatibility rules, fallback behavior).
Runbook: step-by-step canary promotion, smoke checks to run, and rollback playbook for SREs and Solutions Eng.
Customer-facing FAQ: what pinning means for SLAs and how to request de-pinning or bespoke verification.
updates: 2025-03-06: Kickoff meeting with Eng(Runtime), Evals, and Security. Agreed on manifest minimal fields and signature approach.
2025-03-08: Evals delivered first KV-warmup harness PR; found a 7% median latency improvement when prewarming cache for medium sequences.
2025-03-10: Cost-normalization proposal reviewed with Finance; they requested clearer tokenization mapping for multibyte tokens used by some tokenizers.
2025-03-12: Security sketched an HSM-backed signing approach; requested a threat model doc before GA.
2025-03-12: Updated acceptance criteria to require histogram exports and kernel trace attachments in provenance bundle.
open_questions: Which key rotation cadence is acceptable for signed manifests without invalidating existing pinned references?
Do we allow 'composite anchors' that represent a weighted average across hardware families or only single-hardware anchors?
What is the acceptable latency/cost drift threshold to trigger automatic re-verification vs. human review?
Should legacy profiles without full provenance be automatically archived or left discoverable with a 'provenance-missing' warning?
estimated_effort_breakdown: Evals/QA: harness changes and validation workloads - 3 points
Runtime/Serving: pin API + compatibility checks - 2 points
